findings.title: load_formatter_pack: non-callable fn branch has no test
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case in TestLoadFormatterPack: set FORMATTERS = [("a", 42, FormatterKind.COMPAT)] and assert TypeError with match="fn must be callable". The branch at _registry.py:284 is not exercised by any existing test. The bad_kind and malformed_entry tests cover adjacent validation paths but skip this one.

findings.title: run_formatter_safely: write-then-raise case untested; leaked-bytes check is dead on exception path
findings.suggested_fix: The existing test_stdout_write_guard tests write-then-return. The implementation catches Exception first (src/protokit/_cli_utils.py:287), so if a formatter writes to stdout and then raises, the exception path fires and the leaked-bytes check never runs. Add a test with a formatter that does sys.stdout.write("LEAK") then raises RuntimeError; assert exit 2 and error message mentions the exception (not the stdout leak), documenting the ordering contract.

findings.title: reject_quiet_plus_structured: no test for compat history/bisect/ci subcommands with --quiet --format sarif or --quiet --format junit
findings.suggested_fix: TestQuietJsonMutex covers --quiet --format json for all four subcommands but the widened reject_quiet_plus_structured also blocks junit and sarif. No test verifies --quiet --format junit or --quiet --format sarif is rejected for bisect, history, or ci. The existing git_repo fixture makes this easy to add alongside the current json-specific cases.

findings.title: compat history and bisect: no end-to-end CLI test for junit or sarif formatter dispatch
findings.suggested_fix: TestCompatCheckIntegration covers compat check with junit and sarif through CliRunner and XSD/JSON-schema validation. The history and bisect formatters are unit-tested in isolation (test_formatters_junit.py, test_formatters_sarif.py), but the full CLI pipeline for those subcommands with --format junit or --format sarif is not integration-tested. Requires git_repo fixture access; if available, two round-trip tests (history+junit, bisect+sarif) would close this gap.

findings.title: _history_report_to_dict and _bisect_report_to_dict converters are not tested for structural equivalence with pre-refactor JSON shape
findings.suggested_fix: The two private dict-projection functions implement the legacy JSON contract for history/bisect. They are exercised indirectly via the json formatter built-ins tested in test_formatters_builtin.py. The diff comment says "regression contract is structural equivalence with the pre-refactor output" — a direct structural-equivalence test (key-by-key comparison against the old JSON output) would make this contract explicit and catch any future key-shape drift.

residual_risks: pytest-xdist isolation: clear_user_formatters() in autouse fixtures is correct for serial execution. If xdist parallelism is enabled at the module level in future, tests in different workers sharing the same module-level _REGISTRY singleton could interfere. Both new fixture sites implement yield-style autouse correctly for current usage.

run_formatter_safely exception ordering: the exception handler catches Exception (not BaseException), so SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt from a formatter propagate without the leaked-bytes check running. This is likely intentional but undocumented and untested.

Formatter pack import side effects: load_formatter_packs uses importlib.import_module, which executes top-level module code. A malicious or buggy pack could register formatters during import (before FORMATTERS is read) in addition to declaring them in FORMATTERS. The two-phase load in load_formatter_pack would then see a built-in collision on the register_formatter call, but the side-effect registration during import is not rolled back. This is an inherent limitation of the design documented in the plan.
testing_gaps: Non-callable fn branch in load_formatter_pack (src/protokit/formatters/_registry.py:284) — no test exercises TypeError for fn type validation.

Formatter write-then-raise behavior — the existing test covers write-then-return only; the exception-first path in run_formatter_safely means write-then-raise takes the exception error branch, not the leaked-bytes branch, and this ordering is untested.
Widened quiet+structured mutex — TestQuietJsonMutex covers json for all four compat subcommands but does not test junit/sarif rejection for bisect/history/ci.
End-to-end formatter dispatch for history and bisect CLI subcommands — only compat check is integration-tested through CliRunner with XSD/JSON-schema validation.
